category_title: Underprepared writers who procrastinate on topic selection and narrowing
minimal_context: The student is attempting to select and narrow down a topic for a 15-page research paper on a social problem during a summer bridge program.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to select a topic for your 15-page research paper on a social problem. What are you thinking of writing about?

STUDENT: I don't have anything yet. I thought it was boring to choose a specific topic beforehand.

TUTOR: You need to pick something so you can begin working on the assignment.

STUDENT: I guess I didn't really believe that it matters if you narrow down your topic before you start writing.

TUTOR: What do you think will happen if you keep waiting?

STUDENT: I'm just wasting all my time trying to find what I want to write about. It's like the less I work on my paper, the more years I take off my life, but I just can't quit procrastinating.

options.A: Make the student feel welcomed, accepted, and recognized as a valued member of the summer bridge program community.
options.B: Implement program routines, such as signing in and out of the writing sessions each day, to mimic workplace practices.
options.C: Operationalize the curriculum via a single assignment: a 15-page research paper on a social problem of the student's own choosing.
options.D: Demonstrate passion during the summer bridge program and constantly share personal experiences to stimulate, challenge, and motivate the student.
